hook_text: Eighty years later, historians still argue about one decision. Today, you get to weigh the evidence.
clip_script: August 1945. America has a weapon that can destroy a city. Should it use it? One side says yes. Japan's generals refuse to surrender. Invading Japan could cost hundreds of thousands of lives, maybe more. Every week, prisoners and people in occupied Asia are dying. The bomb could end it all fast. The other side says no. The targets are cities full of children. Japan is already beaten, starving and looking for a way out. Scientists who built the bomb begged: show it first, on an empty island. Promise the emperor can stay. Wait for the Soviet Union to join the war. And why bomb Nagasaki just three days later? Historians agree on what happened. They disagree on why, and whether it was right. So be the judge. Weigh the evidence, question the sources, and make your case.
visual_style: A balance scale tipping back and forth; a typed scientists' report stamped June 1945; a map of Japan with two cities circled; a judge's gavel resting beside a stack of documents.
pacing: Balanced back-and-forth rhythm, ending on a direct challenge.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to examine the evidence and build your own argument.
